Vosloorus Ground Force

By: Chuma Kave | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A number of anti-crime groups have sprung up in different townships. They chase down suspects, kick down down doors, arrest. They are effective but are they legal?

Unique Selling Point:
Anti-crime groups performing better than the police.

Summary:
After being gatvol of crime taking place in their townships and where it seemed like nobody cares, in June 2022, a group of Ekurhuleni businesspeople, professionals, community members, and ex-policemen came together and formed an anti-crime NPO called Ekurhuleni Thatha Zone Anti-Crime Unit. The NPO carries “licensed” firearms; some members belong to local security companies.

Every day from 5 pm they hit the streets.

They focus on 4 main areas.

Car hijackings
Drug dealing
GBV
Cellphone theft
And other minor crimes.


This idea was born after one of the townships, Vooslorus, became notorious for daily hijackings and a dumping ground for hijacked victims. The community decided to stand up and do something about it because “the police are under-resourced and you will die waiting for them. If any car is hijacked here we are able to close off the highway immediately and we recover cars within a short space of time”.

They apprehend criminals and hand them over to the police. They investigate drug dealers and conduct sting operations. Women experiencing GBV are able to call the group for help. The NPO believes that their operation has reduced crime drastically and that “we don’t know what our townships would look like if we didn’t have Thatha Zonke”.

The NPO claim they are not breaking any law and work hand in hand with the police.

Further information:
Is this legal and can they be empowered? And, in terms of the Criminal Procedure Act, what are the powers granted to civilians, and to what extent their activities could go beyond the powers?
The feature also investigates if there's a violation of the Private Security Industry Regulation Act and if their actions are tantamount to vigilantism.
What is the relationship between this group, Thatha Zonke, and the local police and what does the law say about this?

Script:


VIZ: Opening Scene: Visuals of people in uniform in what looks like a parade of officers and being addressed + music

Upsound Mandla: The criminals are already on the road…
How many of you have guns?…Your firearm remains concealed.
Your gun must be 45 degrees down….

1. VO: It’s Friday night on Johannesburg’s East Rand.
A 30-strong group of men and women have ditched their weekend PLANS …raided their cupboards for camouflage.. and come together to stand up against THEIR BIGGEST enemy: CRIME.

Upsound Mandla: We don’t want any stories after this… Let us be professional. But, don’t negotiate with those criminals


2. VO: They call themselves Thatha Zonke – which means…suggestively: take ‘em all.

Upsound Mandla: We go as a team, we fight as a team. We win as a team.
Upsound Mandla: These streets of Vosloorus are being hijacked by the criminals. We will force the crime to go down. We are not asking them…we own the streets.

3. VO: In the face of what they feel is a lacklustre response from the police to their plight…this group is highly organised… highly mobilised and putting their own cars, guns…and NECKS… on the line.

Visuals: Cars leaving
Upsound: “Lie down”! “Lie Down!”. Why are you running away?


4. VO: But who…and what… is Thatha Zonke?
How far are they willing to go?
Are they crossing any line?

Visuals: Streets at night
Visuals: Thatha Zonke cars in the streets driving to what seems like a hostel

DIP to black

Visuals: Busy Vosloorus streets during the day

5: V/O: Living in Johannesburg’s Far East Rand is not for the faint-hearted.
With a 9% increase in reported murders in the province last year - makes Ekurhuleni the leader in Gauteng…with Vosloorus officially the kidnapping capital of South Africa.

LINK Claire: A number of anti-crime groups have sprung up in different townships taking on cases and squeezing suspected criminals. And here in Katlehong, Thokoza and Vosloorus, a group of businessmen came together and drew the line.

Upsound Mandla: Our township was burning. All the townships were burning because of these faceless people. They were harassing the community. They thought now they own the townships. To them it was just business as normal.

6: VO: Mandla Nkambule spent 23 years in the police and now runs his own business.
In Thatha Zonke, he’s the Supreme Commander. While it is a registered security company…they see themselves as part of the Community Policing Forum, meant to bridge the gap between police and the people.


Upsound Mandla: CPF is the mother body of all the patrollers but with us, we are there to give the police backup… We are part of CPF, but we are more…ruthless. We don’t negotiate with criminals. ….. ..we are there to fight fire with fire especially when it comes to GBV cases….that’s where we don’t take shit. we go there within seconds.

Claire: An operation like this needs funding

Upsound Mandla: We do everything out of our own pockets. The gear that we are wearing. The firearms that we are using. We bought it ourselves.

7: V/O: Mandla is well aware that getting his hands dirty fighting criminals on the street, might one day mean that he won’t come back home … As a father, husband… and son, he has a lot to lose. And a lot to fight for.

Visuals: Mandla preparing to leave joking around with his son, hugging his mother, Playing with his dogs and stepping inside his car and on the road….

BREATHE

Visuals: The bush drone footage + 4x4 arriving in the bush

Upsound Themba: This place is dangerous. Even the police don't come here willingly, nilly at night. They will never come here. It's us who come in here.

Visuals: Themba inside his bakkie and entering the bush

8: V/O: Commander Bush grew up herding cattle and falling in love with the bush.
For Thatha Zonke he covers the notorious stretch of no-mansland on the egde of Katorus, called Zonkezizwe.
breathe
Here, Commander Bush’s helped to track and rescue several hijacking victims

Upsound Themba: This is about ten square kilometers of nothing…So if you are here, with criminals, your life, you must just pray.

Claire: What are the challenges of fighting crime or patrolling here?

Themba:... maximum discipline. When we are here you don't speak. You keep quiet. When you step on the bush, you don't step on the bush as if you are coming off an elevator. We command you. You follow the command.

Breather


9: VO: Simphiwe Khumalo runs a construction and renewable energy company.
It was when his wife was hijacked, that he drew the line.

Simphiwe: they took all the valuables, laptops, cell phones, and cleaned their bank accounts.

10: VO: He was so fed-up with the lack of action on her case that he joined ThathaZonke, bringing a history of struggle and defiance.

SIMPHIWE - At the back of my mind wanted to say, okay, what happens when a person is hijacked? They take away your freedom. You can't do anything. So crime in general takes away your freedom.

11: VO: Thatha Zonke was forged from fire of the notorious 1990s… when these streets saw some of the most violent conflicts in the country’s transition to democacy.

Visuals: Thokoza violence - Gallo images

SEGUE TO KHUMALO STREET

Claire Link - Khumalo Street: The freedom we currently enjoy in this country was paid for by blood and tears and this street, Khumalo Street, was right in the centre of that struggle. Something that still inspires these men. (2967)

Visuals - Khumalo Street + Thokoza drone

Upsound Simphiwe: It is the idea of securing the gains that you have caught after the 1994 election…we must now fight and engage every resources that we have in making sure that we defend the freedom….

12: VO: As a young boy Simphiwe ran the streets as a member of the area’s Self Defence Unit. He eventually became one of the youngest people to be granted amnesty before the historic Truth and Reconciliation Commission…for his subversive acts in the liberation struggle.

Visuals: Simphiwe before the TRC
Upsound: Simphiwe 1998: I was given the task every time they launch an attack, I go first and…if they were police, I’d say a signal. My role was make sure the guns are cleaned.

Claire: When you reflect…as a child handling weapons for the struggle…?

Simphiwe: It shouldn’t have happened…..but it natured us to take care of our communities because we’ve been there and defended the community when we were young.

13: V/O: They have a hotline number and a Facebook page … no crime is too big or too small: they started out with hijackings…now it’s housebreaking…even petty crimes.


BREATHER

14 VO: But is Thatha Zonke…going beyond the call of duty for a community policing forum… are they on the right side of the law?

Claire: Do they have a right and a space to operate?

Upsound Themba Masuku: the law actually allows communities to organize themselves, but they must work with the police…

15 VO: In the African Policing Civilian Oversight Forum, Themba Masuku has seen groups like these mushroom … around the country.

Upsound Themba Masuku: So your community patrollers, your your neighbourhood watch…they don't have special powers. So they cannot, for example, they cannot engage in covert operations, they cannot investigate crime, they cannot search, they cannot enter into people's homes.

VISUALS: Mandla driving in the streets + doing stop & search + chasing suspected drug dealers (during the day)

16: VO: So .. they’re forced to obey the law while trying to be creative about meeting real needs.

Upsound: Themba Masuku: Some of those limitations are designed to respect everyone's rights because everybody's got a right to their dignity.

Visuals: Thatha Zonke turning a shack upside down looking for drugs.

BREATHER

Visuals: Helicopter, members arriving, laughing…and some eating (9052)

17: V/O: Tonight’s patrol has been planned for weeks.. some members join the operation straight from work.

Visuals: Members lining up and being addressed by their commander

Upsound Mandla: I would like to welcome every member who is here tonight. Who is going to pray for us?
Upsound Prayer female member: We trust you Lord with our lives...please grant us protection.

LINK CLAIRE: It’s Friday night and the beginning of the weekend can be very unpredictable for our group it means leaving nothing to chance and making sure they also mentally prepared for the battle that lies ahead.

Upsound Mandla: We are not going out there to play. Those criminals are not playing with the community…so we don’t play with them.

Upsound Mandla: We must hit them. We must saturate that place.

Visuals: Cars flooding the streets + natural sound

18: VO: In the streets … they want to make their presence felt

Visuals: Stop & search - street

19: VO: The Commander’s unit receives a distress call via the hotline.

Upsound Mandla: Robbery in progress. Let’s move

20: VO: By the time we arrive, the suspects are gone. Not a case of robbery as it turns out, but a man terrorising a woman because of a dispute with her brother.

Upsound Mandla: Do you know where he lives?

21: VO: When the police officers arrive they suggest a way forward.

Police: You can go to the police and open a case or do a court interdict.

22: VO: A visibly unhappy commander cannot hide his frustration.

Upsound Mandla: We wanted to go there now but the cops are taking a soft stance…

Link Claire: So about 30+ members of the Thatha Zonke team and their aim is to stop and search anyone that looks suspicious and checking that are potentially hijacked and tonight we have the police with us and their presence makes this operation legitimate.

23: VO: For Thatha Zonke crime-fighting also means meeting social needs.. being the fathers…uncles… and aunts, where those are not around.

Upsound: How old are you?
Visuals of two 16 years old in a tavern and told to go home “Go home”
Visuals of a young man high on drugs and being loaded at the back of the van “where did you buy these drugs”

24: VO: in an abandoned car parked by a tavern…a shocking sight

Upsound Mandla: Where is the mother of this baby?

25: VO: The mother eventually makes her way outside… her baby alone

Visuals - baby
Visuals of the commander helping the mother to cover the baby and kissing the baby

26: VO: The mood shifts… again.

Visuals: Commander roughing up a drunk man who is part of the people who came with the baby.

27: VO: As the night winds down.. there’s no compromise…
Visuals: Members still saturating the streets…no time to slow down.

28: Because the mission is bigger than themselves…and their limited resources and powers

Visuals: Thatha Zonke women on the streets








PROMOS

PROMOS
21 SEC
Visuals: Themba Meso + street search / boots on the ground.
LINK: They hit the streets every night, conduct investigations, and raids, chase down and apprehend suspects.
Upsound: Themba Meso If you are doing crime we are going to meet with you one way or the other, If we have to come and arrest you, we will come and arrest you. No fear, no favour. (CLIP 2880 (14:25 - 14:44)
LINK: We investigate a self-funded anti-crime unit in the East Rand that claims more success than the police (3001)

21 Sec
LINK: Just like any other township in South Africa, this area of Vosloorus, Katlehong and Thokoza had the residents feeling powerless and criminals in charge…
Upsound Mandla: We are dealing straight with Vosloorus today. Those robberies, kidnappings…we must hit them…
LINK: A group of men and women came together and said enough! (2981)
Upsound Mandla: We do not negotiate with a criminal (3036).

11 Seconds
VO: They claim that they will go further than even the police will dare… But is one self-styled community anti-crime unit in Gauteng, taking things too far?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A number of anti-crime groups have sprung up in different townships. They chase down suspects, kick down down doors, arrest. They are effective but are they legal?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Anti-crime groups performing better than the police.
metadata.Summary: After being gatvol of crime taking place in their townships and where it seemed like nobody cares, in June 2022, a group of Ekurhuleni businesspeople, professionals, community members, and ex-policemen came together and formed an anti-crime NPO called Ekurhuleni Thatha Zone Anti-Crime Unit. The NPO carries “licensed” firearms; some members belong to local security companies. Every day from 5 pm they hit the streets. They focus on 4 main areas. Car hijackings Drug dealing GBV Cellphone theft And other minor crimes. This idea was born after one of the townships, Vooslorus, became notorious for daily hijackings and a dumping ground for hijacked victims. The community decided to stand up and do something about it because “the police are under-resourced and you will die waiting for them. If any car is hijacked here we are able to close off the highway immediately and we recover cars within a short space of time”. They apprehend criminals and hand them over to the police. They investigate drug dealers and conduct sting operations. Women experiencing GBV are able to call the group for help. The NPO believes that their operation has reduced crime drastically and that “we don’t know what our townships would look like if we didn’t have Thatha Zonke”. The NPO claim they are not breaking any law and work hand in hand with the police.
metadata.Further information: Is this legal and can they be empowered? And, in terms of the Criminal Procedure Act, what are the powers granted to civilians, and to what extent their activities could go beyond the powers? The feature also investigates if there's a violation of the Private Security Industry Regulation Act and if their actions are tantamount to vigilantism. What is the relationship between this group, Thatha Zonke, and the local police and what does the law say about this?
